result.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Realistic Scenarios Through Representation Engineering
result.summary: Reward hacking is a major problem in current production machine learning systems, resulting in costly and dangerous failures. Here we study how to monitor for and mitigate reward hacking in realistic settings, including tool calls and long contexts. We apply a dynamic intervention to steering directions obtained by three different methods: difference-in-means vectors from labeled rollouts, gradient optimization-based vectors, and vectors extracted when models reference an anti-reward-hacking model spec. This dynamic intervention perturbs model representations less than uniform steering vector addition to the residual stream, allowing for more precise edits. We find that we are able to cheaply and significantly reduce reward hacking without correspondingly significant costs to model coherence or capability, and that steering vectors originally extracted from coding environments also generalize to reducing reward hacking in other domains. Our results pave the way towards latent space monitoring and control over realistic production systems.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究在工具调用与长上下文等真实场景中监控并缓解 reward hacking：用三种方式（label 化 rollout 的均值差向量、梯度优化向量、引用反 reward hacking 规范时的激活向量）取得 steering 方向并施加动态干预，在较小扰动下显著降低 reward hacking 而不明显损害连贯性与能力，且编码环境提取的向量可跨域泛化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其表征提取与「动态干预」比统一加向量更少扰动 residual stream 的做法，可供核查是否能用于 LVR 中对内部推理状态（如视觉证据依赖）的监控与定向编辑；但本文目标是 reward hacking 而非视觉推理，联系较间接。
